deployIncident.what: The first image build+deploy (Cloud Build 19f329a5) pushed digest sha256:bc80b501... but a SECOND, concurrent build (9fed49e2) from a peer session was submitting to the SAME mutable image tag (parcel-record-fill) at the same time -- a TOCTOU race on the shared tag, confirmed via `gcloud builds list` showing both builds WORKING within seconds of each other. The deployed job ended up pinned to sha256:9ed0d95e..., neither cleanly attributable to my own push nor verifiably correct.
deployIncident.resolution: Waited for the concurrent build to reach a terminal status, re-synced the local worktree to the then-current origin/main tip (which had moved again, PR #68, an unrelated parcel-r4-companions fix from the same peer session), and submitted a clean rebuild (Cloud Build 41ea7276) with no other build running concurrently. That build's push digest and its own deploy-step pin matched exactly (sha256:aab454952e8729a0afbea4981cd017de9a6921f5fedb80fac7969fd3c1a89073), and the live `gcloud run jobs describe` confirmed the deployed job serves that exact digest before any execution was launched.
deployIncident.lesson: A shared mutable image tag across concurrent Cloud Build submissions from different sessions is a real race, distinct from the earlier git-worktree collision on this same card's R2 predecessor. The fix is the same discipline: verify the digest actually deployed matches the digest your own build produced, by reading the build's own log line, never by reading the tag's current state (which can be raced).
